summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted for melena and found to have acute blood loss anemia and a supratherapeutic INR of 4.0, likely due to recent endoscopic biopsy for residual gastric adenocarcinoma. He received one unit of packed red blood cells and IV iron for iron deficiency anemia. Warfarin was held and a heparin bridge initiated until the INR normalized, after which warfarin was restarted at 5 mg daily. GI did not recommend urgent endoscopy, and there was no evidence of ongoing bleeding. His heart failure was managed with cautious reintroduction of torsemide. He was evaluated for surgical risk given his mechanical valve, cirrhosis, and cardiac history, and was deemed high risk but without contraindications. He was discharged home with services, on a stable hemoglobin of 8.0, INR of 2.2, and a plan for oncology follow-up regarding possible partial gastrectomy.
problems: Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
